title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors and Senior Executives, Senior Executives being the Managing Director, other key management personnel as defined under the Corporations Act who hold executive roles, direct reports to the Managing Director who are not KMP, and others selected by the Board. This tier carries the Blackout Periods, the 12 month short-term trading ban, the prior consent requirement for dealing and for Hedging, and the post-trade confirmation duty.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors, Senior Executives and employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. Employees who are not Restricted Persons may deal at any time provided they notify the Company Secretary before and after the transaction and hold no inside information; they are only 'strongly advised' not to deal during Blackout Periods and are not subject to the 12 month short-term trading ban.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Associates of Restricted Persons, including a company or trust controlled by the Restricted Person, a spouse, dependent children, a close relative and a person acting in concert with the Restricted Person. Connected Persons are subject to the same Blackout Periods, short-term trading ban, consent requirement and Hedging rules, and Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure they do not breach the policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging)

windows.end_anchor: 10:00am AEDT on the ASX trading day following the day on which the Company's half-yearly results are released to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Blackout Period from time to time. No criteria, notification method, duration or confidentiality rule is stated. Separately, the Board may in its discretion determine that persons other than Restricted Persons are prohibited from Hedging.

rules.detail: The definition of Company securities is confined to Company-issued instruments (shares, debentures, units of shares and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares), and 'deal' is confined to subscribing, purchasing, selling and agreements to do so, so a bank-written option is not itself a Company security. Paragraph 15 nonetheless regulates derivatives economically by requiring prior consent for any transaction or arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of a holding, with no venue limit, so an over-the-counter put and call over vested unrestricted shares require the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board for the Managing Director) and post-trade confirmation.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.

rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons need only notify the Company Secretary before and after a transaction; the paragraph 15 consent requirement binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons only, and the Board would have to make a specific determination to prohibit Hedging by anyone else.
rules.evidence: Employees other than Restricted Persons may deal in Company securities at any time if the employee notifies the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and after the transaction has occurred, providing confirmation of the trading.

rules.detail: Hedging is not banned outright for ordinary shareholdings: it requires the prior consent of the Managing Director (or the Chairman of the Board where the Managing Director is hedging), and subsequent confirmation of the trading, including trading by a Connected Person. The policy records that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged', so consent is discretionary and may be refused or made conditional without reasons.
rules.evidence: Generally speaking Hedging is discouraged and is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company, which covers unvested options and rights held under those plans. The only route around it would be the paragraph 14 exceptional circumstances discretion.
rules.evidence: Hedging ... is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: The same explicit prohibition applies while securities remain part of participation in a securities-based remuneration plan or scheme. Shares received on exercise may not be sold other than in accordance with the policy's procedures, so shares still held under plan arrangements should be treated as outside the collar.
rules.evidence: explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Paragraph 15 binds Restricted Persons and Connected Persons. Employees outside those tiers may hedge subject only to the paragraph 18 notification duty and the insider trading prohibition, unless and until the Board exercises its discretion to prohibit them.
rules.evidence: The Board may, in its discretion, determine that other persons are prohibited from Hedging.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. Each is an arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of a holding and so falls within Hedging, requiring prior consent and post-trade confirmation. A structure that in substance sells the shares within 12 months would also engage the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy. A short position would in practice be caught by the 12 month short-term trading ban for Restricted Persons and by the Front Page Test general principle.
Securities lending is not named, and the definition of 'deal' is confined to subscribing for, purchasing or selling Company securities or agreeing to do those things.

CFDs are not named. A CFD written against an existing holding is an arrangement limiting economic risk and so is Hedging requiring prior consent; a speculative CFD closed out within 12 months would breach the short-term trading ban and would be difficult to reconcile with the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging)

rules.detail: There is no margin lending clause. The nearest provision is the general principle that personal trading must not use broker credit and must settle on relevant exchange settlement terms and industry standards, which bars buying Company securities on credit extended by a broker. It is directed at settlement of trades rather than at a third party lender taking security over an existing holding, and the accompanying principle that trading be on a scale reflecting the individual's ability to fund and maintain the portfolio points the same way.
rules.evidence: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards;

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned, is not within the definition of 'deal', and triggers no notification or consent obligation.

The policy contains no secured financing provision: no prohibition, no consent requirement, no disclosure obligation and no treatment of a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period. Only the broker credit principle in paragraph 11(f) and the perception-based Front Page Test bear on the question.

An unusually long 12 month intention test binding Restricted Persons and Connected Persons at all times, catching both a purchase with a view to resale and a sale with a view to repurchase within 12 months. The only carve-out is the sale of shares acquired on conversion of a security where the combined holding periods of the security and the resulting shares exceed 12 months. Paragraph 14 allows the Managing Director or Chairman to approve dealings that would otherwise be prohibited, so this ban is in principle waivable.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.

clearance.approver: Paragraphs 11(h) and 15 require the prior approval or consent of the Managing Director, or the Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director. Paragraph 16 instead routes the request through the Company Secretary, who seeks consent from the Chairman of the Board as Authorising Officer, or from the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee where the Chairman of the Board is the person dealing.
clearance.post_trade_to: Chairman of the Board (or Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee) and the Company Secretary, by transaction confirmation; the Managing Director or Chairman also receives subsequent confirmation of Hedging trading, including by a Connected Person; directors must notify the Company Secretary in writing for ASIC and ASX notification
clearance.post_trade_deadline: after dealing; a director must notify the ASX within 5 days after any change in the director's relevant interest
clearance.evidence: A request for consent to deal in Company securities will be answered as soon as practicable. The Authorising Officer may refuse to consent to the proposed dealing or impose conditions on the dealing at their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any refusal or condition. In all cases, the dealing consented to must occur within 5 business days following approval, otherwise the consent is no longer effective and fresh consent must be sought.

clearance.approver: The same approver as for the associated Restricted Person; the Restricted Person notifies the Company Secretary of any proposed dealing by a Connected Person and consent is sought on their behalf
clearance.post_trade_to: Managing Director or Chairman of the Board (confirmation of Hedging trading by a Connected Person); Chairman of the Board and Company Secretary (transaction confirmation)
clearance.evidence: notify the Company Secretary of their proposed dealing (including any proposed dealing by one of their Connected Persons) so that the Company Secretary may seek on their behalf consent from the Chairman of the Board

carve_outs: the sale of shares after they have been acquired through the conversion of a security (e.g. exercise of an option or right), provided that the combined periods over which the security and resulting shares were held exceeds 12 months

exemption_authority: Paragraph 14: in exceptional circumstances the Managing Director, or the Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director, has discretion to approve dealings during a Blackout Period 'or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy'. This is a broad waiver power that on its face can relieve against the short-term trading ban and the prohibition on Hedging plan securities, assessed case by case in the absolute discretion of the Board, and it may include severe financial hardship or a court order or court enforceable undertaking. Any such approval must be provided by electronic delivery via email and the paragraph 16 notification and procedural requirements still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person or Connected Person may not deal in Company securities or enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their holdings of Company securities (known as Hedging) without the prior consent of the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director before commencing the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging is a consent-gated activity rather than a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over ordinary vested shares can be approved; the consent is discretionary and the policy adds that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, charges, mortgages or pledges over Company securities, and no related disclosure obligation.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited or made subject to consent, so the funded element turns on the general principles and on whatever conditions the approver imposes rather than on an express bar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: do not utilise broker credit - relevant exchange settlement terms must apply on all occasions and all transactions must be settled according to industry standards.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only leverage-related principle in the policy bars trading on broker credit, so the bank should structure the facility as a third party loan secured on an existing holding rather than as credit used to acquire or settle Company securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and Connected Persons may never engage in short term trading of any Company securities. In general, the purchase of securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The tenor of the collar, and any roll, early termination or physical settlement, should exceed 12 months, since a written call that is exercised inside that period looks like a sale with a view to a repurchase or a short-dated disposal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in exceptional circumstances the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board in the case of the Managing Director, has discretion to approve dealings in Company securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies, the waiver power extends beyond blackout relief to any dealing otherwise prohibited, so even the plan-securities hedging bar and the 12 month rule are in principle waivable on a case-by-case basis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Paragraphs 11(h) and 15 require consent from the Managing Director (or the Chairman for the Managing Director), while paragraph 16 requires the Company Secretary to seek consent from the Chairman of the Board as Authorising Officer (or the Chairman of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chairman of the Board).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names two different approval routes for the same dealing, so consent for a collar should be obtained from both the Managing Director and the Chairman of the Board through the Company Secretary to be safe.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Authorising Officer may refuse to consent to the proposed dealing or impose conditions on the dealing at their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any refusal or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The company can attach conditions to a collar approval, for example on size, tenor or disclosure, and those conditions must be reflected in the derivative and loan documentation before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In all cases, the dealing consented to must occur within 5 business days following approval, otherwise the consent is no longer effective and fresh consent must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and loan documentation must be ready to sign before consent is sought, since the approval expires five business days after it is granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: "Company securities" includes any shares in the Company, debentures (including convertible notes) issued by the Company, units of shares in the Company and rights or options to acquire or subscribe for shares in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Third party derivatives are not themselves Company securities, so a bank-written put and call are caught by the paragraph 15 Hedging test rather than by the dealing and Blackout provisions, and the analysis turns on economic effect rather than on instrument type.

bespoke_clauses.clause: avoid personal trading that would not satisfy the Front Page Test, being: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the individual taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's funded collar is exactly the kind of transaction that attracts perception scrutiny, so the approver may refuse consent on this ground alone even though nothing in the policy prohibits it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must also provide the Managing Director or Chairman of the Board ... with subsequent confirmation of the trading that has occurred (including trading by one of their Connected Persons). ... a director must notify the ASX within 5 days after any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging by a Restricted Person must be confirmed to the company after the event and a director's change in relevant interest reaches the ASX within five days, so the collar will not stay private.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also applies to Connected Persons of all Restricted Persons, being each of their respective associates (including a company or trust controlled by the Restricted Person, a spouse, dependent children, a close relative, a person acting in concert with the Restricted Person, etc).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a controlled company or trust does not avoid the consent, short-term trading or confirmation requirements.

summary: A funded collar is possible for a NEXTDC director or Senior Executive, but only with discretionary consent and over ordinary vested shares. Hedging is defined by economic effect and is consent-gated rather than banned: a Restricted Person may not enter into transactions or arrangements limiting the economic risk of their holdings without the prior consent of the Managing Director (the Chairman of the Board where the Managing Director is hedging), must confirm the trading afterwards, and the policy records that Hedging is 'generally speaking discouraged' and is explicitly prohibited in relation to participation in any securities-based remuneration plan or scheme, so the collar must reference shares held outside those plan arrangements. The loan leg is not obstructed, since the policy says nothing about margin lending, secured financing or encumbrances; the only leverage-related principle bars the use of broker credit in settling trades, which a third party facility secured on an existing holding does not engage. The main practical constraints are the 12 month short-term trading ban, which argues for a tenor and unwind window comfortably beyond 12 months, the Blackout Periods running from 31 December and 30 June until the morning after results, the five business day life of a consent, the approver's unreviewable power to refuse or impose conditions without reasons, and the Front Page Test perception standard. Unusually, paragraph 14 gives the Managing Director or Chairman a discretion to approve not only blackout dealings but 'other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy', so even the plan-securities hedging bar and the 12 month rule are in principle waivable.
